newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end gyrating to a BHP swing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end gyrating to a BHP swing.

text.p: SPI futures 2232 -15 US 30yr cl 7.05 +.03
*Stocks gyrated in a 20 point band as BHP swung widely after its first quarter result. Turnover 291.20 million, value A$556.51 million, 996 stocks traded, 326 steady, 320 up, 350 down.
Australian stocks ended lower on Friday as the share market gyrated within a 20 point band as market heavyweight BHP swung widely after investors digested the resource giant's first quarter result.

At 4.30 p.m. (0630 GMT), the All Ordinaries index ended 6.3 points lower at 2240.80, but flirted in positive zones throughout the day. The September share price index had a harder fall, 15 points down at 2232 and widening the discount to the underlying index to 8.8 points.
Brokers said investors were mixed about the BHP result, which sent its share price and overall market into a spasm.

"The market has been following BHP up and down all day," one Sydney broker said. BHP reported a 22.8 percent fall in net profit to A$287 million in the three months to August 31, which was within market expectations.
"BHP has certainly been the focus, it was pounded from all quarters after the result, but some fresh buying took place in the afternoon to see its come back a bit," the broker said.

Shares in BHP swung in a 43 cents range between positive and negative territory all day and had the broader market following in its wake. Brokers said that despite the weak resources there were still some firm gains in the industrial sector.

"The resources have really dictated this week but don't forget some of the industrials have performed well over the week. The banks have risen quite firmly this week as investors seem to be chasing yield stocks in this market," a broker said.
Chemicals, retail, packaging and insurance sectors were amongst the few indices to post modest gains today.
However, brokers said metal prices are still likely to command the market direction next week.
In other markets, Australian bonds ended softer amid mild profit-taking as the market showed some caution ahead of the FOMC meeting next Tuesday, where U.S. rate hikes are possible.

The Australian dollar finished a sombre week in a minor upbeat note as the resilience of support defeated repeated attempts to extend the correction. At 5.15 p.m. (0715 GMT), the local dollar was quoted at US$0.7912/17.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade was steady. Total options traded 50,183 (49,430) covering 278 issues.
Turnover in September SPI contracts totalled 6,766 (6,954).
